item.research_question: Can high-entropy layered rare earth hydroxychlorides be synthesized, and how do their structural parameters, elemental distribution, and thermal stability compare to low-entropy analogues?
item.material_system: High-entropy layered rare earth hydroxychlorides: (Sm,Eu,Gd,Y,Er)2(OH)5Cl, (Eu,Gd,Tb,Y,Er)2(OH)5Cl, (Eu,Gd,Dy,Y,Er)2(OH)5Cl, (Eu,Gd,Y,Er,Yb)2(OH)5Cl; Medium-entropy: (Eu,Gd,Er)2(OH)5Cl, (Eu,Gd,Y,Er)2(OH)5Cl; Binary/Ternary: EuEr, EuErGd, YEuErGd, Eu_MW, Tb_MW, Er_MW
item.processing_route: Microwave-assisted homogeneous hydrolysis under hydrothermal conditions; 0.1 M REE chloride solutions mixed with 1 M NaCl and 0.14 M hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) at a molar ratio of REE3+:NaCl:HMT = 1:10:1.4; treated in a Teflon autoclave at 140 °C for 30 min (900 W) after 5 min heating at 1800 W; 30% filling degree
item.test_conditions: XRD (5–90° 2θ, CuKα); EDX mapping (20 kV); FT-IR (3650–3330 cm−1 range); Luminescence (532 nm laser, ~2 mW); Thermal analysis (air, 250 mL/min flow, 20 °C/min heating rate up to 1200 °C)
key_findings: Unit cell parameters correlate linearly with average rare earth cation radii (0.868 < R2 < 0.982).
Configurational entropy (ΔSconf) for five-cation samples exceeded 1.5R, classifying them as high-entropy compounds.
Ternary and quaternary samples showed ΔSconf between 1R and 1.5R, classifying them as medium-entropy.
EDX mapping confirmed even distribution of rare earth elements on a submicron scale.
Efficient energy transfer between europium and other cations was observed via luminescence quenching or enhancement.
Thermal decomposition occurred in three stages: water elimination (<170 °C), oxide/oxychloride formation (170–700 °C), and chlorine elimination (>1050 °C).
High-entropy samples exhibited thermal stability similar to low-entropy binary and single-cation analogues.
Samples containing Nd3+ showed deviations in unit cell parameters due to impurity phase formation (Nd(OH)3).
item.mechanism: The linear correlation between cation radius and unit cell parameters indicates solid solution formation without phase separation. The entropy-stabilization effect is evidenced by the synthesis of single-phase HE_Yb_MW, where single-cation ytterbium hydroxychloride is otherwise unstable. Thermal stability remains comparable to low-entropy systems because the reaction entropy (ΔSdecomp) is not significantly affected by cation composition, as configurational entropy contributes equally to both initial and final decomposition products.
item.limitations: The refinement of unit cell parameters for layered rare earth hydroxynitrates is impossible due to stochastic coordination of nitrate anions. Significant differences in cation radii (e.g., in Nd-containing samples) can lead to segregation of individual phases and impurity formation. The study notes that high-entropy layered hydroxides cannot be classified as entropy-stabilized in terms of thermal decomposition.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that understanding the thermal behavior of metal hydroxides is of primary importance for the synthesis of multicomponent catalytic materials and predicting their functionality.
quotes: The average rare earth cation radii correlated linearly with the unit cell parameters (0.868 < R2 < 0.982) of the high-entropy layered rare earth hydroxychlorides.
The thermal stability of the high-entropy layered rare earth hydroxychlorides was similar to that of individual hydroxychlorides and their binary solid solutions.
This fact provides evidence for the entropy-stabilisation effect in the HE_Yb_MW sample.
